1	# Resources
2	
3	Resources represent the data objects available through a connector (e.g., Salesforce Account, Contact, Opportunity). Each resource supports a set of CRUD operations.
4	
5	> Full command syntax and options: [uip-commands.md — Integration Service](../uip-commands.md#integration-service-is). Domain-specific usage patterns are shown inline below.
6	
7	## Contents
8	- Listing and Describing Resources
9	- Response Fields
10	- Describe Response
11	- Describe Failures
12	- Parent-Field-Driven Custom Fields (api-type ObjectActions)
13	- Execute Operations
14	- Pagination
15	- Execute Error Handling
16	
17	For reference field resolution (simple refs, dependency chains, required field validation), see [reference-resolution.md](reference-resolution.md).
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Listing and Describing Resources
22	
23	**Always pass `--connection-id`** to get connection-specific metadata including custom objects and fields. Without it, only standard objects/fields are returned.
24	
25	## Response Fields
26	
27	| Field | Description |
28	|---|---|
29	| **`Name`** | Resource identifier (used in commands) |
30	| `DisplayName` | Human-readable name |
31	| `Path` | API path for this resource |
32	| `Type` | Resource type (standard, custom) |
33	| `SubType` | Sub-type (e.g., method, entity) |
34	
35	## Describe Response
36	
37	The describe command returns metadata from the raw API. The output depends on whether `--operation` is provided.
38	
39	### Without `--operation` — operation summary
40	
41	Returns which operations the resource supports:
42	
43	| Field | Description |
44	|---|---|
45	| **`availableOperations`** | List of operations — each with `method` (GET/POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE), `name` (Create/List/etc.), `description`, `curated` (display name) |
46	| **`hint`** | Instructs to use `--operation` for field details |
47	
48	### With `--operation` — per-operation field detail
49	
50	Returns the full field breakdown for the specified operation:
51	
52	| Field | Description |
53	|---|---|
54	| **`operation`** | Operation info — `method`, `name`, `description`, `path`, `curated` display name |
55	| **`parameters`** | Path and query parameters (NOT body fields) — each with `name`, `type` (path/query), `dataType`, `required`, `defaultValue`, `reference` |
56	| **`requestFields`** | Fields to send in `--body` — each with `name`, `type`, `displayName`, `required`, `description`, `reference`, `enum` |
57	| **`responseFields`** | Fields returned in the response — each with `name`, `type`, `displayName` |
58	
59	> **Always use `--operation`** to get actionable field detail. Without it you only see which operations exist.
60	
61	### Key field properties
62	
63	- **`required: true`** — field must be provided in `--body` or `--query`. Do NOT skip.
64	- **`reference`** — field value must be looked up from another resource. See [reference-resolution.md](reference-resolution.md). When baking a static value for a reference field, also emit `designTimeMetadata.designTimeLookups` so the edit-UI renders a label — see [reference-resolution.md — Static Reference-Value Labeling](reference-resolution.md#static-reference-value-labeling).
65	- **`enum`** — field only accepts the listed values (e.g., `["low", "normal", "high"]`).
66	
67	Results are cached locally. Use `--refresh` to bypass cache after re-auth or schema changes.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Describe Failures
72	
73	Some resources return an error on describe. This is a **server-side metadata gap** — do not retry with `--refresh`.
74	
75	**Recovery:**
76	
77	1. **Skip describe entirely** — do not waste calls retrying.
78	2. **Infer fields from user context** — use the field names and values the user provided in their request.
79	3. **Infer reference fields from naming** — see [reference-resolution.md — Inferring References Without Describe](reference-resolution.md#inferring-references-without-describe).
80	4. **Attempt execute directly** — let the server validate. If a field is rejected, read the error and adjust.
81	
82	---
83	
84	## Parent-Field-Driven Custom Fields (api-type ObjectActions)
85	
86	For connectors whose required fields depend on parent-field selections (Jira `GenerateSchema` keyed off project + issue type, Salesforce SOQL `GenerateQuerySchema` keyed off the query string, Dataservice V3 `FetchObjectMetadataTenant` keyed off `tenantEntityName`), the base `describe` returns only base fields. To preview the full required-field set the runtime will see, pass parent values via `-f, --field`:
87	
88	```bash
89	# Jira: project + issue type → custom fields (GET, query-param tokens)
90	uip is resources describe uipath-atlassian-jira curated_create_issue \
91	  --connection-id "<id>" --operation Create \
92	  -f fields.project.key=ENGCE \
93	  -f fields.issuetype.id=3 \
94	  --output json
95	
96	# Salesforce SOQL: query string → response columns (POST, body token)
97	uip is resources describe uipath-salesforce-sfdc query_records \
98	  --connection-id "<id>" --operation Create \
99	  -f query="SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE Status = 'Active'" \
100	  --output json
101	```
102	
103	What it does — runs the matching api-type ObjectAction against the IS Element Service (same path Studio Web's dispatcher uses), then merges the response into `requestFields` per the action's `onSuccess.remapConfiguration`. Use it before validating required fields to catch project- or operation-specific mandatory fields the base describe can't see.
104	
105	| Flag | Notes |
106	|------|-------|
107	| `-f, --field <name=value>` | Repeatable. Token names match `apiConfiguration.url` and `apiConfiguration.body` placeholders verbatim — no `_sub_` encoding (encoding only applies when caching parent values for runtime replay; see [activities.md — Custom Fields](activities.md#custom-fields-objectactionsactiontypeapi)). |
108	| `--action <name>` | Optional. Disambiguates when more than one api-type action could match the field set. |
109	
110	Requires `--connection-id` and `--operation`. Cache is bypassed when `--field` is supplied — the action response varies per parent-field combination. The merge mode (`replace` / `append` / `prepend` / `noop`) comes from the action's `remapConfiguration.input`; for Jira `GenerateSchema` it is `replace`.
111	
112	When no api-type action's `rules[]` are satisfied by the supplied fields, the CLI errors with `No api-type ObjectAction matched for fields [...]`. List the operation's actions from the describe output's `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` (or top-level `objectActions[]` for older shapes) to see which fields each action requires.
113	
114	---
115	
116	## Execute Operations
117	
118	| Verb | Description | `--body` | `--query` |
119	|---|---|---|---|
120	| `create` | Create a new record | Yes | No |
121	| `list` | Retrieve multiple records | No | Optional (`limit=10&offset=0`) |
122	| `get` | Get a single record by ID | No | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
123	| `update` | Partial update (PATCH) | Yes | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
124	| `delete` | Delete a record | No | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
125	| `replace` | Full replacement (PUT) | Yes | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
126	
127	> **Update** (PATCH) = change specific fields. **Replace** (PUT) = overwrite entire record. Default to **Update** unless the user says "replace" or "overwrite".
128	
129	### Filtering Results with `--output-filter`
130	
131	Use the global `--output-filter` flag with a JMESPath expression to extract specific fields from large responses if possible via JMESPath.
132	
133	```bash
134	# Extract only id, name, and email from a user list
135	uip is resources execute list "<CONNECTOR_KEY>" "<OBJECT_NAME>" \
136	  --connection-id "<CONNECTION_ID>" \
137	  --output json \
138	  --output-filter "Data[].{id: id, name: name, email: profile.email}"
139	```
140	
141	Common JMESPath patterns:
142	
143	| Pattern | Effect |
144	|---|---|
145	| `Data[]` | Return all records (unwrap the Data envelope) |
146	| `Data[].name` | Return just the `name` field from each record |
147	| `Data[].{id: id, name: name}` | Return selected fields as objects |
148	| `Data[?status=='active']` | Filter records by field value |
149	| `Data[0]` | Return only the first record |
150	
151	---
152	
153	## Pagination
154	
155	`uip is resources execute list` may not return all results in a single call. **Always check for pagination** when searching for a specific item or listing all items.
156	
157	### Pagination rules
158	
159	1. **Always check `Data.Pagination`** — every `list` response may contain pagination state. Never assume a single page contains all results.
160	2. **Complete the pagination loop** — when searching for a specific item, keep paginating until `Data.Pagination.HasMore` is `"false"` or the item is found. Do NOT abandon pagination mid-loop to try alternative APIs (e.g., search endpoints, admin endpoints, HTTP fallback).
161	3. **Stop early on match** — if you find the target item in the current page, stop. No need to fetch remaining pages.
162	4. **Report not-found only after exhausting all pages** — only conclude an item does not exist after `HasMore` is `"false"` and every page has been checked.
163	
164	### Connector pagination
165	
166	Most IS connectors use the `elements-*` pagination protocol. The CLI returns pagination state nested inside `Data.Pagination`:
167	
168	- **`Data.Pagination.HasMore`**: `"true"` or `"false"` — indicates if more pages exist
169	- **`Data.Pagination.NextPageToken`**: the token value to use for the next page
170	
171	**IMPORTANT:** The query parameter name is `nextPage` (NOT `nextPageToken`). Pass the value from `Data.Pagination.NextPageToken` as `--query "nextPage=<value>"`.
172	
173	```bash
174	# First page (do not pass pageSize unless the user explicitly requests a specific page size)
175	uip is resources execute list "<connector-key>" "<resource>" \
176	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
177	# → Check Data.Pagination.HasMore and Data.Pagination.NextPageToken in the JSON response
178	
179	# Subsequent pages — use nextPage as the query param name (NOT nextPageToken)
180	uip is resources execute list "<connector-key>" "<resource>" \
181	  --connection-id "<id>" --query "nextPage=<value-from-NextPageToken>" --output json
182	# → Continue until Data.Pagination.HasMore is "false" or target item is found
183	```
184	
185	Example response:
186	```json
187	{
188	  "Result": "Success",
189	  "Code": "ExecuteOperation",
190	  "Data": {
191	    "items": [ ... ],
192	    "Pagination": {
193	      "HasMore": "true",
194	      "NextPageToken": "eyJwYWdl..."
195	    }
196	  }
197	}
198	```
199	
200	### Anti-patterns
201	
202	- **Do NOT check `Data.nextPage`** — pagination lives at `Data.Pagination.HasMore` and `Data.Pagination.NextPageToken`, not at `Data.nextPage`.
203	- **Do NOT abandon pagination to try other APIs** — if you are paginating through `conversations` to find a channel, do not stop mid-loop to call `admin_conversations_search`, `search_all`, or `search_messages`. Complete the loop first.
204	- **Do NOT conclude "not found" after one page** — a single page may return only a fraction of the total results. Always check `Data.Pagination.HasMore` before concluding.
205	
206	### Query-param pagination (offset/limit)
207	
208	Some resources support `offset`/`limit` via `--query`:
209	
210	```bash
211	uip is resources execute list "<connector-key>" "<object>" \
212	  --connection-id "<id>" --query "limit=50&offset=0" --output json
213	# → next page: --query "limit=50&offset=50"
214	```
215	
216	Stop when the result set is empty or smaller than the limit.
217	
218	### HTTP connector exception
219	
220	Connectors with key `uipath-uipath-http` do NOT use the `elements-*` pagination headers. These depend on vendor-specific pagination. Handle on a case-by-case basis.
221	
222	---
223	
224	## Execute Error Handling
225	
226	When an execute command fails, the CLI returns:
227	- **`Message`**: HTTP status (e.g., `400 Bad Request`)
228	- **`Instructions`**: The raw vendor error response body as JSON
229	
230	### How to diagnose failures
231	
232	1. **Read `Message`** — the HTTP status code tells you the category (400 = bad request, 403 = forbidden, 404 = not found, etc.)
233	2. **Read `Instructions`** — the raw vendor error body tells you WHAT specifically failed (invalid field, missing required value, permission denied, etc.)
234	3. **Use discovery to fix** — run `describe` to get valid field names, run `list` to get valid values for reference fields
235	4. **Retry with fixes** — apply the specific correction and re-execute (max 2 retries)
236	
237	For the full recovery loop, see [agent-workflow.md — Error Recovery](agent-workflow.md#error-recovery).
238

1	# Activities
2	
3	Activities are pre-built actions available for each connector (e.g., "Send Message", "Create Issue"). They represent specific operations the connector supports. Activities include both **actions** (non-trigger) and **triggers** (event listeners).
4	
5	> Full command syntax and options: [uip-commands.md — Integration Service](../uip-commands.md#integration-service-is). Domain-specific usage patterns are shown inline below.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## List Activities (Non-Trigger)
10	
11	Use the connector **Key**, not the display name. For Salesforce, the canonical key is `uipath-salesforce-sfdc`; do not pass `salesforce` or `uipath-salesforce` to activity commands.
12	
13	```bash
14	uip is activities list "<connector-key>" --output json
15	```
16	
17	```bash
18	uip is activities list "uipath-salesforce-sfdc" --output json
19	```
20	
21	This lists **non-trigger activities only** (actions, not event listeners).
22	
23	## List Trigger Activities
24	
25	```bash
26	uip is activities list "<connector-key>" --triggers --output json
27	```
28	
29	```bash
30	uip is activities list "uipath-salesforce-sfdc" --triggers --output json
31	```
32	
33	The `--triggers` flag filters to **trigger activities only** (`isTrigger=true`). These represent events the connector can fire (e.g., "Record Created", "Record Updated").
34	
35	The **Operation** field on trigger activities indicates the trigger type:
36	- **CREATED** / **UPDATED** / **DELETED** — CRUD event triggers (require an intermediate "objects" step to discover which objects support the operation)
37	- Other values — custom event triggers (skip directly to metadata)
38	
39	> When a trigger activity is selected, proceed to [triggers.md](triggers.md) for the trigger metadata workflow.
40	
41	## Response Fields
42	
43	| Field | Description |
44	|---|---|
45	| **`Name`** | Activity identifier |
46	| `DisplayName` | Human-readable name (e.g., "HTTP Request", "Send Message") |
47	| `Description` | What the activity does |
48	| **`ObjectName`** | The resource object this activity operates on (use as `<object-name>` in trigger describe for non-CRUD triggers) |
49	| `MethodName` | HTTP method used (GET, POST, etc.) |
50	| **`Operation`** | Operation type — for triggers, this is the event type (CREATED, UPDATED, DELETED, or custom) |
51	| `IsCurated` | Whether this is a curated/recommended activity |
52	
53	---
54	
55	## When to Use Activities vs Resources vs Triggers
56	
57	- **Activities** = named actions (e.g., "Send Email"). Discovered via `is activities list`.
58	- **Triggers** = event listeners (e.g., "Record Created"). Discovered via `is activities list --triggers`. Metadata via `is triggers objects` / `is triggers describe`. See [triggers.md](triggers.md).
59	- **Resources** = data objects with CRUD (e.g., "Account"). Discovered via `is resources list`. Executed via `is resources run <verb>`.
60	
61	> After listing activities, present the available actions to the user. Activities provide context for what a connector can do — use this to guide which resource operations, triggers, or workflow actions to pursue.
62	
63	---
64	
65	## Filter Trees (CEQL)
66	
67	Some IS activities — most notably **List All Records** and other list/query operations — accept a server-side filter expressed in **CEQL** (Connector Expression Query Language). As with trigger filters (which compile to JMESPath), CEQL filters are authored as a **structured filter tree** and the CLI compiles them to a CEQL string. Authoring as a tree keeps the CLI and Studio Web in lockstep so the activity round-trips cleanly when re-opened in SW.
68	
69	### Contract — three signals from IS metadata
70	
71	The CLI reads the live IS metadata response and uses three signals to wire the filter:
72	
73	1. **The activity supports CEQL** when one of its `parameters` declares `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. That parameter's `name` is the connector-specific key the compiled CEQL string is sent under — most commonly `where`, but **not always** (e.g. Salesforce uses `q`). Activities with no such parameter do not support server-side filtering — pass no `filter` and filter downstream.
74	2. **A field is filterable** when its IS metadata entry has `searchable: true`. Type alone does not gate it — the connector flags fields explicitly. Fields without `searchable: true` are rejected by the CLI even if they look like primitives.
75	3. **Permitted operators** for the field are listed under `searchableOperators`. **Connector-side identifier** for the field in CEQL is `searchableNames[0]` when present (some connectors expose a friendly `name` but require a different identifier in the query string).
76	
77	### What the CLI persists from a single `filter` input
78	
79	- **Runtime side** — the compiled CEQL string lands at `inputs.detail.queryParameters.<filterParamName>` where `<filterParamName>` is the FilterBuilder parameter's name from the IS metadata (often `where`).
80	- **Design-time side** — the structured tree is embedded under `inputs.detail.configuration`'s `essentialConfiguration.savedFilterTrees.<filterParamName>`. Studio Web reads this on open to re-render the filter widget; without it the filter UI shows up empty even though the runtime call still works.
81	
82	Pass `filter` (the structured tree) and the CLI emits both halves in lockstep. Passing both `filter` and `queryParameters.<filterParamName>` is rejected at validation time — single source of truth.
83	
84	### Tree shape
85	
86	Identical to the trigger filter tree — the same `FilterTree` / `Filter` / `WorkflowValue` types are used; only the compiler output (CEQL vs JMESPath) differs.
87	
88	```jsonc
89	{
90	  "groupOperator": 0,             // 0 = And, 1 = Or — combines sibling filters/groups
91	  "index": 0,                     // ordering index within parent (root is 0)
92	  "filters": [                    // leaf conditions at this level
93	    {
94	      "id": "<fieldName>",        // resource field name from `is resources describe`
95	      "operator": "<Operator>",   // PascalCase, see operator table below
96	      "value": {
97	        "value": <typed value>,   // string / number / boolean / ISO-8601 date-time / array
98	        "rawString": "\"...\"",   // verbatim user-entered text (with quotes for strings)
99	        "isLiteral": true         // literals only — expression values are not yet supported
100	      }
101	    }
102	  ],
103	  "groups": []                    // optional: nested subgroups (same shape as root)
104	}
105	```
106	
107	A no-op filter — used when the user wants to list all records without restriction — is `null` or `{"groupOperator": null, "index": 0, "filters": []}`. Prefer **omitting** the `filter` field entirely.
108	
109	### Compiled CEQL output
110	
111	The CLI compiles each leaf to `<field> <op> <value>` (or `<field> <function>` for null checks) and joins siblings with the group operator. String values are wrapped in single quotes; booleans, numerics, and enums are passed bare.
112	
113	| Operator | CEQL token | Notes |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| `Equals` | `=` | |
116	| `NotEquals` | `!=` | |
117	| `LessThan` / `LessThanOrEqual` / `GreaterThan` / `GreaterThanOrEqual` | `<` / `<=` / `>` / `>=` | Numeric / date-time |
118	| `Contains` / `NotContains` | `Contains` / `Not Contains` | Substring (string) |
119	| `StartsWith` / `NotStartsWith` / `EndsWith` / `NotEndsWith` | `Starts With` / `Not Starts With` / `Ends With` / `Not Ends With` | String |
120	| `Like` / `NotLike` | `Like` / `Not Like` | Pattern match (connector-specific) |
121	| `In` / `NotIn` | `In` / `Not In` | Membership — `value.value` is a list; rendered as `(v1, v2, …)` |
122	| `IsNull` / `IsNotNull` | `Is Null` / `Is Not Null` | No `value` needed |
123	| `Is` / `IsNot` | `=` against literal `true` / `false` | Boolean shortcut |
124	
125	Logical operators between siblings:
126	
127	| `groupOperator` | CEQL token |
128	|---|---|
129	| `0` (And) | ` AND ` |
130	| `1` (Or) | ` OR ` |
131	
132	### Examples
133	
134	**Active accounts only:**
135	
136	```json
137	{
138	  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
139	  "filters": [
140	    { "id": "Status", "operator": "Equals",
141	      "value": { "value": "Active", "rawString": "\"Active\"", "isLiteral": true } }
142	  ]
143	}
144	```
145	→ CEQL: `Status = 'Active'`
146	
147	**Score ≥ 80 AND Region in (EMEA, APAC):**
148	
149	```json
150	{
151	  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
152	  "filters": [
153	    { "id": "Score", "operator": "GreaterThanOrEqual",
154	      "value": { "value": 80, "rawString": "80", "isLiteral": true } },
155	    { "id": "Region", "operator": "In",
156	      "value": { "value": ["EMEA", "APAC"], "rawString": "[\"EMEA\",\"APAC\"]", "isLiteral": true } }
157	  ]
158	}
159	```
160	→ CEQL: `Score >= 80 AND Region In ('EMEA', 'APAC')`
161	
162	**Subject contains "urgent" AND (owner = me OR owner is null):**
163	
164	```json
165	{
166	  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
167	  "filters": [
168	    { "id": "Subject", "operator": "Contains",
169	      "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }
170	  ],
171	  "groups": [
172	    {
173	      "groupOperator": 1, "index": 1,
174	      "filters": [
175	        { "id": "OwnerId", "operator": "Equals",
176	          "value": { "value": "${me.id}", "rawString": "\"${me.id}\"", "isLiteral": false } },
177	        { "id": "OwnerId", "operator": "IsNull" }
178	      ]
179	    }
180	  ]
181	}
182	```
183	→ CEQL: `Subject Contains 'urgent' AND (OwnerId = ${me.id} OR OwnerId Is Null)`. Non-literal values (`isLiteral: false`) are emitted as `${expression}` placeholders for runtime resolution.
184	
185	### How to build a CEQL filter tree
186	
187	1. Run `uip is resources describe "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" --connection-id "<id>" --operation List` to read the resource's metadata.
188	2. **Confirm CEQL is supported** for this operation: at least one entry under `parameters` must carry `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. If none does, the activity does not support server-side filtering — omit `filter` and filter downstream (e.g. with a Script node).
189	3. **Pick filterable fields** from `fields[]` where `searchable: true`. Other fields will be rejected by the CLI at configure time even if they look like primitives.
190	4. For each leaf, pick an operator from the field's `searchableOperators` list (when present). Date-time fields take ISO-8601 strings; enums take the literal enum value.
191	5. Use the field's `name` as the leaf `id`. The CLI rewrites it to `searchableNames[0]` when emitting CEQL if the connector declares one — you don't need to use the alias yourself.
192	6. Build one leaf per condition; place multiple conditions under the same `groupOperator` (0 for AND, 1 for OR). Use nested `groups` for mixed AND/OR.
193	7. Wrap values in a `WorkflowValue` object with `value`, `rawString`, `isLiteral`. Strings, numbers, booleans, dates, and arrays are all valid `value` types; only `isLiteral: true` is currently supported by activity-side compilation.
194	
195	### What NOT to generate
196	
197	| Invalid input | Why it fails | Valid replacement |
198	|---|---|---|
199	| `"filter": "Status = 'Active'"` | Bare CEQL string — `filter` must be an object. | Structured tree with `filters: [...]`. |
200	| `"filterExpression": "..."` | That field is reserved for the trigger (JMESPath) path. | Use `filter` (CEQL tree) for activities. |
201	| `{ "operator": "equals", ... }` | Operator is case-sensitive. | `"operator": "Equals"` |
202	| `{ "value": "Active" }` on a leaf | Bare string — must be wrapped in the `WorkflowValue` object. | `{ "value": { "value": "Active", "rawString": "\"Active\"", "isLiteral": true } }` |
203	| `{ "id": "fields.Status", ... }` | `fields.` prefix — use the bare field name from `is resources describe`. | `{ "id": "Status", ... }` |
204	| `{ "id": "<field without searchable: true>", ... }` | The CLI checks `searchable` on the IS metadata entry; non-searchable fields are rejected even if their type looks filterable. | Pick a field where `searchable: true`. |
205	| `"queryParameters": { "where": "..." }` alongside `filter` | Hardcoding `where` assumes that's the FilterBuilder param name — it isn't always (Salesforce uses `q`, etc.). | Pass `filter` only; the CLI discovers the right param name from `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. |
206	| `In` operator with a single value not in a list | `In` expects an array `value`. | Use `Equals`, or pass `value: ["one"]`. |
207	
208	## Custom Fields (`objectActions[ActionType=Api]`)
209	
210	Connectors with extensible/custom fields (Jira project+issuetype → custom Jira fields, Mailchimp list_id → audience merge fields, Salesforce custom objects) expose `Api`-type entries under `objectActions[]`. Each entry's `apiConfiguration.url`/`body` carries `{token}` placeholders naming the parent fields. The runtime replays the ObjectAction with cached parent values to fetch the connector-specific custom-field schema.
211	
212	**For Maestro flows**, this lives on the activity node as `essentialConfiguration.customFieldsRequestDetails`. Authoring contract → [uipath-maestro-flow connector/impl.md Step 6c](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md).
213	
214	Shape:
215	
216	```json
217	"customFieldsRequestDetails": {
218	  "objectActionName": "GenerateSchema",
219	  "parameterValues": [["fields_sub_project_sub_key", "ENGCE"], ...]
220	}
221	```
222	
223	camelCase inner keys, `parameterValues` as `[key, value]` tuples (Studio Web emits `Map<string,string|null>` via `Array.from(entries())`). Object-map form rejected by the CLI.

commands.result_summary:
uip maestro flow node configure                         
Configure a connector or managed HTTP node with connection and method details.
Run this after 'node add' — populates inputs.detail and creates workflow bindings.
Use 'node list' to find the node ID.

CONNECTOR ACTIVITIES (type uipath.connector.*, NOT *.trigger.*)
  Required: connectionId, folderKey, method, endpoint.
  Generic activities (manifest activityType='Generic', e.g. *.insert-record,
    *.list-records) also require objectName. Discover with:
      uip is resources list <connector-key> --operation <op> --connection-id <uuid>
      uip is resources describe <connector-key> <object> --operation <op> --connection-id <uuid>
  Curated activities: get method/endpoint from connectorMethodInfo in 'registry get'.
  Optional: bodyParameters, queryParameters, pathParameters, filter,
            customFieldsRequestDetails ({ objectActionName, parameterValues: [[k,v],...] });
  Examples:
    --detail '{"connectionId":"<uuid>","folderKey":"<uuid>","method":"POST","endpoint":"/issues","bodyParameters":{"summary":"Bug"}}'
    --detail '{"connectionId":"<uuid>","folderKey":"<uuid>","method":"POST","endpoint":"/Account","objectName":"Account","bodyParameters":{"Name":"Acme"}}'
  Cross-node bindings (referencing another node's output) require the
  "$vars." prefix inside the "=js:" expression — the bare form
  (e.g. "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id") resolves to undefined at runtime:
    --detail '{"connectionId":"<uuid>","folderKey":"<uuid>","method":"POST","endpoint":"/Account","bodyParameters":{"recordId":"=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"}}'

CONNECTOR TRIGGERS (type uipath.connector.trigger.*)
  Required: connectionId, folderKey, eventMode (e.g. 'polling' or 'webhook').
  Generic triggers (manifest activityType='GenericTrigger', e.g. Data Fabric
    *.record-created) also require objectName — the object to subscribe to.
    Discover with: uip is triggers objects <connector-key> <eventType> --connection-id <uuid>
  Optional: eventParameters, queryParameters, pathParameters,
            filter (structured FilterTree, not a raw expression).
  Discover eventMode with:
    uip is triggers describe <connector-key> <eventType> <object> --connection-id <uuid>
  Examples:
    --detail '{"connectionId":"<uuid>","folderKey":"<uuid>","eventMode":"polling"}'
    --detail '{"connectionId":"<uuid>","folderKey":"<uuid>","eventMode":"webhooks","objectName":"MyEntity"}'

CONNECTOR WAIT-FOR EVENTS (type uipath.connector.event.*)
  Mid-flow Receive Task that pauses execution until the event fires.
  Same detail shape as connector triggers — only activityType differs internally.
  Required: connectionId, folderKey, eventMode (e.g. 'polling' or 'webhooks').
  Generic event nodes also require objectName (same rule as triggers).
  Optional: eventParameters, queryParameters, pathParameters,
            filter (structured FilterTree, not a raw expression).
  Discover eventMode with:
    uip is triggers describe <connector-key> <eventType> <object> --connection-id <uuid>
  Example:
    --detail '{"connectionId":"<uuid>","folderKey":"<uuid>","eventMode":"polling","queryParameters":{"repo":"cli"}}'

MANAGED HTTP NODES (type core.action.http.v2)
  Two authentication modes — set via the 'authentication' key:

  Connector mode (authentication='connector'):
    Uses an Integration Service connection for auth.
    Required: authentication, method (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/OPTIONS/HEAD),
              connectionId (target connector connection UUID),
              folderKey, targetConnector (e.g. uipath-microsoft-outlook365)
    Optional: url (path appended to connector base URL), headers, query, body
    Example:
      --detail '{"authentication":"connector","targetConnector":"uipath-microsoft-outlook365","connectionId":"<uuid>","folderKey":"<uuid>","method":"GET","url":"/me"}'

1	# Connector Activity Nodes — Implementation
2	
3	How to configure connector activity nodes: connection binding, enriched metadata, reference field resolution, and debugging. Connection bindings are emitted by `uip maestro flow node configure` into the flow's top-level `bindings[]`; `bindings_v2.json` is regenerated from them at debug/pack time and should never be hand-edited.
4	
5	For generic node/edge add, remove, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). This guide covers the connector-specific configuration workflow that must follow the generic node add.
6	
7	## How Connector Nodes Differ from OOTB
8	
9	1. **Connection binding required** — every connector node needs an IS connection (OAuth, API key, etc.) authored in the flow's top-level `bindings[]` (which the CLI regenerates into `bindings_v2.json` at debug/pack time). Without it, the node cannot authenticate.
10	2. **Enriched metadata via `--connection-id`** — call `registry get` with `--connection-id` to get connection-aware field metadata. Without it, only base fields are returned — custom fields, dynamic enums, and reference resolution are missing.
11	3. **`inputs.detail` object** — connector nodes store operation-specific configuration in `inputs.detail`, populated by `uip maestro flow node configure`:
12	   - `connectionId` — the bound IS connection UUID
13	   - `connectionFolderKey` — the Orchestrator folder key in the authored `.flow` file. `node configure --detail` accepts `folderKey` as input and writes it back as `connectionFolderKey`.
14	   - `method` — HTTP method from `registry get` → `connectorMethodInfo.method` (e.g., `POST`)
15	   - `endpoint` — API path. Read `connectorMethodInfo.path` (from `registry get`) or `availableOperations[].path` (from `is resources describe`).
16	   - `objectName` — required for generic activities (see below). The API object name (e.g. `"Opportunity"`); ignored for concrete nodes.
17	   - `bodyParameters` — field-value pairs for the request body. Read field names from `inputDefinition.fields[].name` (`registry get`) or `requestFields[].name` (`is resources describe`).
18	   - `queryParameters` — field-value pairs for query string parameters. Read from `connectorMethodInfo.parameters[]` where `type: query` (`registry get`) or `parameters[]` (`is resources describe`).
19	   - `pathParameters` — field-value pairs for path placeholders in `endpoint` (e.g. `{conversationsInfoId}`). Read from `connectorMethodInfo.parameters[]` where `type: path` (`registry get`) or `parameters[]` (`is resources describe`).
20	   - `filter` — structured FilterBuilder tree for list/query operations. See Step 6a.
21	   - `customFieldsRequestDetails` — design-time cache for connectors with an api-type ObjectAction at top-level `objectActions[]` OR `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` (e.g. Jira `GenerateSchema`, Dataservice V3 `FetchObjectMetadataTenant`). camelCase keys; `parameterValues` as `[key, value]` tuples. See Step 6c.
22	   - `multipartParameters` — derived from IS metadata params where `type === "multipart"`. Array of `{name, dataType, value?}`. Pass file values via `--detail.bodyParameters.<name>`; `node configure` moves file-typed values into the matching `multipartParameters[i].value` slot (matched by `name`). String-typed entries — including the body aggregator field whose name is given by `inputMetadata.multipart.bodyFieldName` — stay in `bodyParameters`.
23	   - `inputMetadata` — auto-derived. `{type: "multipart", multipart: {bodyFieldName}}` when multipart params exist; `{operation: "list", pagination: {maxPageSize}}` for list operations. Driven by `methodInfo.parameters` + `methodInfo.operation`.

27	## Generic vs Concrete Activities
28	
29	Connector nodes come in two flavors:
30	
31	- **Concrete** — the node type encodes a specific object + operation (e.g. `uipath.connector.uipath-atlassian-jira.curated_create_issue`). `inputDefinition.fields[]` is populated; `method` and `endpoint` are fixed.
32	- **Generic** — the node type encodes only the operation (e.g. `uipath.connector.uipath-salesforce-sfdc.list-records`, `…insert-record`, `…update-record`). `inputDefinition` is `{}`; the node needs an extra `objectName` in `--detail`, and `method` / `endpoint` come from `is resources describe`.
33	
34	To classify a node, read `Node.form.sections[0].fields[0].componentProps.connectorDetail.configuration` from the `registry get` response, parse it as JSON, and check `activityType`. `"Generic"` → run Step 2a to discover `objectName` (and capture `operation` from the same marker for the `--operation` flag in Step 3). Anything else → skip Step 2a.
35

37	## Critical: Connector Definition Must Include `form`
38	
39	> Connector definitions in `definitions[]` are CLI-owned (see [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node)) — `uip maestro flow node add` copies them verbatim from the registry, and you should never hand-write or hand-edit them. If `node configure` fails with `No instanceParameters found in definition`, the definition in `definitions[]` is missing the `form` field — typically because the local registry cache is stale (the definition was copied in before the CLI started emitting `form`). Recovery: `uip maestro flow registry pull --force`, delete the stale `definitions[]` entry, re-run `uip maestro flow node add <file> <node-type>` so the CLI re-copies the definition with `form`. Do not paste `form` in by hand — re-running `node add` is the supported path.
40	
41	## No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration
42	
43	If you cannot run `node configure` (no live connection, sandbox forbids it, the user asked for planning only):
44	
45	1. Confirm the connector operation exists: `uip maestro flow registry search <keyword>` and `registry get <node-type>` (see [cli-commands.md — registry](../../../../shared/cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-registry) for the `search` output shape).
46	2. Add the connector node with `uip maestro flow node add <file> <node-type> --output json`. This is still required — it inserts the node and copies the definition into `definitions[]`. **Inside a loop body?** Add `--parent <LOOP_NODE_ID>` — see [loop/impl.md](../loop/impl.md).
47	3. Write the planned `--detail` payload to a separate file (e.g. `<nodeId>.detail.json`) with placeholder values for missing connection/folder UUIDs. Do **not** put a partial `inputs.detail` on the node.
48	4. **The node will not pass `flow validate` until `node configure` is run.** Surface this explicitly in your completion report under "Missing connections" or "Open questions" — do not let the user discover it via a validation failure later.
49	
50	Do not replace a registered connector operation with `core.logic.mock` because configuration cannot run. Mocks are only for genuinely unknown, unpublished, or not-yet-built non-connector resources. A real connector node added via `node add` but unconfigured preserves the registered connector key that Studio Web, reviewers, and downstream tooling need.
51	
52	When piping `--output json` into `python`, `jq`, or another parser, do not merge stderr into stdout. The CLI may emit diagnostic lines such as "Tool factory already registered..." before the JSON on stderr; use `2>/dev/null` for parse-only probes or capture stderr separately.
53	
54	## Configuration Workflow
55	
56	Follow these steps for every connector node.
57	
58	### Step 1 — Fetch and bind a connection
59	
60	Extract the connector key from the node type (`uipath.connector.<connector-key>.<activity-name>`).
61	
62	Discovery call is **always**:
63	
64	```bash
65	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
66	```
67	
68	`connections list` returns `Data` as a flat array. Do **not** parse `Data.Connections` or `Data.Items`; those wrapper objects are not part of the CLI JSON contract. Read each candidate from `Data[]` and use PascalCase fields:
69	
70	```json
71	{
72	  "Data": [
73	    {
74	      "Id": "<connection-id>",
75	      "Name": "<display-name>",
76	      "State": "Enabled",
77	      "IsDefault": "Yes",
78	      "Folder": "<folder-name>",
79	      "FolderKey": "<folder-key>"
80	    }
81	  ]
82	}
83	```
84	
85	Use `Data[i].Id` as the `--connection-id` value and `Data[i].FolderKey` as the `folderKey` value in `node configure --detail`.
86	
87	> **MUST READ before any `uip is connections ...` call:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md). Single source of truth for selection rules (auto-select, personal workspace), BYOA filtering, empty-result recovery, ping verification.
88	
89	End state: a healthy connection `Id` + `FolderKey` for Step 2 (`registry get --connection-id`) and Step 6 (`node configure --detail`).
90	
91	### Step 2 — Get enriched node definitions with connection
92	
93	Call `registry get` with `--connection-id` to fetch connection-aware metadata including custom fields:
94	
95	```bash
96	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --connection-id <connection-id> --output json
97	```
98	
99	This returns enriched `inputDefinition.fields` and `outputDefinition.fields` with accurate type, required, description, enum, and `reference` info. Without `--connection-id`, only standard/base fields are returned.
100	
101	The response also includes `connectorMethodInfo` with the real HTTP `method` (e.g. `GET`, `POST`) and `path` template (e.g. `/ConversationsInfo/{conversationsInfoId}`). **Save `connectorMethodInfo.method` and `connectorMethodInfo.path`** — you must pass them to `node configure` later as `method` and `endpoint`.
102	
103	> **For generic activities, `connectorMethodInfo` is empty.** Method and endpoint are object-specific and only resolve once Step 2a picks an `objectName`; Step 3 then surfaces them via `availableOperations[]`. Don't try to derive them from the manifest alone.
104	
105	### Step 2a — Discover the object name (generic activities only)
106	
107	Skip this step for concrete activities — they encode the object in the node type. For generic activities (`activityType: "Generic"`), list the connection's catalog and pick the object the user wants to act on.
108	
109	```bash
110	uip is resources list "<connector-key>" --connection-id "<connection-id>" --output json \
111	  --output-filter "[?contains(DisplayName,'<search>')].{Name:Name,Path:Path,Custom:Custom}"
112	```
113	
114	- `Name` — what `--detail.objectName` accepts. Case-sensitive (e.g. `"Opportunity"`, not `"opportunity"`). Don't substitute `DisplayName`.
115	- `Path` — API endpoint suffix (e.g. `/Opportunity`). Pair with the operation's HTTP method (Step 3) for `endpoint`.
116	- `Custom` — `true` for tenant-defined objects.
117	
118	### Step 3 — Describe the resource and read full metadata
119	
120	Run `is resources describe` to fetch and cache the full operation metadata, then **read the cached metadata file** for complete field details including descriptions, types, references, and query/path parameters. The describe summary omits some of this.
121	
122	**Read `<objectName>` from the node definition in `definitions[]` (written by `node add`) — do not guess it from the node-type suffix.**
123	
124	```bash
125	# 1. Describe to trigger fetch + cache (objectName = the activity's API object, NOT the node-type suffix)
126	#    Read <objectName> from the node definition FIRST (see note below) — do not batch this
127	#    call with `node add` / `registry get`; those calls PRODUCE the objectName this one consumes.
128	uip is resources describe "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" \
129	  --connection-id "<id>" --operation Create --output json
130	# -> response includes metadataFile path
131	
132	# 2. Read the full cached metadata
133	cat <metadataFile path from response>
134	```
135	
136	> **`<objectName>` is the activity's API object name, not the node-type's trailing segment — and NOT a case-conversion of it.** Read it from the node definition copied into `definitions[]` by `node add`: `model.context[]` entry `{name:"objectName", value:"…"}` (or the `objectName` field inside the `configuration` `=jsonString:` blob). Never derive it by transforming the node-type suffix — kebab→snake (`send-email` → `send_email`) and kebab→Pascal are both guesses and both 404. Example: node type `…google-gmail.send-email` has objectName `SendEmail` (not `send_email`); `…teams.send-bot-direct-message` has objectName `bot_direct_messages` (not `send-bot-direct-message`). A 404 means wrong objectName — re-read it from the definition and retry; do NOT treat the 404 as "describe unavailable" and skip the step. Skipping describe loses `requestFields[].reference.filterPattern` and other IS-level metadata that `registry get` does not carry (see Step 4).
137	>
138	> **Sequence, don't parallelize, the objectName-dependent calls.** `<objectName>` is an OUTPUT of `node add` (it lands in `definitions[]`). Read that value before calling `is resources describe` — do not place `describe` in the same parallel Bash batch as `node add` or `registry get`, or you'll have nothing to pass but a guess. This is the failure mode behind the snake-case 404 above.
139	
140	The full metadata contains:
141	- **`availableOperations[].method`** and **`availableOperations[].path`** — HTTP method and API endpoint path. Same value as `connectorMethodInfo.method` / `.path` from `registry get`.
142	- **`parameters`** — query and path parameters (may include required params not in `requestFields`, e.g. `send_as` for Slack). Parameters carry `reference` objects too — scan them in Step 4 exactly like body fields.
143	- **`requestFields`** — body fields with `name`, `type`, `required`, `description`, and `reference` objects for ID resolution. Pair these field names with the `path` above (e.g. `messageToSend` for Slack `/send_message_to_channel_v2`).
144	- **`responseFields`** — response schema
145	
146	### Step 3a — Resolve parent-field-driven custom fields (api-type ObjectActions)
147	
148	**Run whenever the activity has a parent-field-driven schema** — an api-type ObjectAction in `objectActions[]` or `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` (see Step 6c's support table). Applies to **every** operation with such an action — Create/Edit/Update for parent-driven required body fields AND Get/Retrieve/Query for the response-schema fields downstream nodes will reference. The base `describe` returns only static metadata; this step runs the matching ObjectAction against the live connection so the cache you author in Step 6c is a replay of a real call, not a fabrication.
149	
150	Pass parent values via `-f, --field` — see [/uipath:uipath-platform — resources.md > Parent-Field-Driven Custom Fields (api-type ObjectActions)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md#parent-field-driven-custom-fields-api-type-objectactions) for the full procedure, flag table, merge semantics, and error recovery.
151	
152	> **Skipping is not free even when the runtime call works.** For Get/Retrieve the upstream API returns data regardless — runtime stays green. The fetch is what makes Step 6c's `customFieldsRequestDetails` honest: without it, Studio Web has no schema to render the activity's custom fields, and any downstream `$vars.<thisNode>.output.<custom-field>` resolves to undefined. `flow validate` does not catch this — it surfaces as silent design-time corruption (MST-9107-class).
153	
154	Run this before Step 5 (validate required fields) and reuse the same parent-field values in Step 6c's `customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues` (with the encoded keys).
155	
156	### Step 4 — Resolve reference fields
157	
158	Check **BOTH `requestFields` AND `parameters`** from the metadata for entries with a `reference` object — these require ID lookup from the connector's live data. Use `uip is resources run list` to resolve them:
159	
160	> **References are NOT body-field-only.** Query and path parameters carry `reference` objects too, and on some connectors the activity's PRIMARY input is a required **path parameter** whose `reference` is the design-time lookup behind a Studio Web dropdown. Scanning only `requestFields` misses it — the node then configures and passes `flow validate` with an unverified value and 404s at runtime. The same `reference` blocks appear on `connectorMethodInfo.parameters[]` in `registry get` output (with or without `--connection-id`) — when projecting parameter metadata for inspection, always include the `reference` key, not just `name`/`required`/`design.component`.
161	
162	> **Resolve every reference field freshly, against the current `--connection-id`, immediately before `node configure` (Step 6)** — even if you think you already know the ID from a previous flow. Reference IDs are connection-scoped and reused values fault silently at runtime. See [Reference IDs Are Connection-Scoped (CRITICAL)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/reference-resolution.md#reference-ids-are-connection-scoped-critical) for the full mechanism and failure mode, and the top-level Anti-Patterns in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md).
163	
164	```bash
165	# Example: resolve Slack channel "#test-slack" to its ID
166	uip is resources run list "uipath-salesforce-slack" "curated_channels?types=public_channel,private_channel" \
167	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
168	# -> { "id": "C1234567890", "name": "test-slack" }
169	```
170	
171	The `<id>` in `--connection-id "<id>"` MUST be the connection bound to **this** flow (the one picked in Step 1), not any other connection you've used in another flow. Use the resolved IDs (not display names) — from this very `run list` call — in the flow's node `inputs`. When multiple matches exist, ask the user, with one option per match plus **"Something else"** as the last option (see the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md)).
172	
173	> **Zero matches on a user-supplied value** — if the completed lookup (`Data.Pagination.HasMore` is `"false"`) finds no entry matching a value the user provided, do NOT configure the node with it silently. Ask the user, presenting the closest candidates as options plus **"Something else"** as the last option (see the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md)). Proceed with the unverified value only if the user confirms it.
174	
175	> **Filter server-side before paginating.** If the field's `reference` carries a `filterPattern` (e.g. Teams `userId`: `"$filter=startswith(userPrincipalName,'{filter}')"`), substitute the search term for `{filter}` and pass the result as `--query` — one targeted call instead of walking a large directory. `filterPattern` appears only in `is resources describe` output; the flow `registry get` reference object strips it (keeps only `objectName`/`lookupValue`/`lookupNames`/`path`/`childPath`), so read it from the Step 3 describe metadata. Guessed params (`searchTerm=`/`where=`/`filter=`) are silently ignored. See [reference-resolution.md — Search References (filterPattern)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/reference-resolution.md#search-references-filterpattern).
176	
177	> **Paginate only when there is no `filterPattern`.** Use `Data.Pagination.HasMore` / `NextPageToken` with `--query "nextPage=<token>"`. Short-circuit on match. Do NOT conclude "not found" until `HasMore` is `"false"`. See [resources.md#pagination](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md#pagination).
178	
179	**Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — Integration Service — resources.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md) for the full reference-resolution workflow** (pagination, describe failures, fallbacks).
180	
181	### Step 5 — Validate required fields
182	
183	**Check every required field** — both `requestFields` and `parameters` where `required: true` — against what the user provided. This is a hard gate — do NOT proceed to building until all required fields have values. For query/path parameters with a `defaultValue`, use the default if the user didn't specify one.
184	
185	1. Collect all required fields from the metadata (`requestFields` + `parameters`)
186	2. For each required field, check if the user's prompt contains a value
187	3. If any required field is missing and has no `defaultValue`, **ask the user** before proceeding — list the missing fields with their `displayName` and what kind of value is expected. Free-form input is appropriate when the value space is open-ended (channel names, message bodies, IDs); when a finite set of sensible values exists, present them as options per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md).
188	4. Only after all required fields are accounted for, proceed to building
189	
190	> **Do NOT guess or skip missing required fields.** A missing required field will cause a runtime error. It is always better to ask than to assume.
191	
192	> **For connectors with api-type ObjectActions, run Step 3a first.** Base `describe` does not surface custom required fields driven by project / issue type / query / tenant entity. Use `-f, --field name=value` to fetch the connection-and-parent-field-specific schema before validating.
193	
194	### Step 5b — Wire outputs from previous nodes
195	
196	When a connector node's input field needs a value produced by an upstream node (e.g. the `Id` returned by a Create activity becomes the `recordId` for a Get-by-Id activity), the value MUST use the canonical expression form:
197	
198	```
199	"=js:$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output.<field>"
200	```
201	
202	Examples in `inputs.detail`:
203	
204	```jsonc
205	"queryParameters": {
206	  "recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"
207	},
208	"bodyParameters": {
209	  "ParentId":  "=js:$vars.queryAccounts1.output[0].Id",
210	  "BankName":  "HDFC Bank",
211	  "Note":      "=js:`Linked from run ${$metadata.instanceId}`"
212	}
213	```
214	
215	> **The `=js:` prefix is REQUIRED on every `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` reference inside `bodyParameters`, `queryParameters`, and `pathParameters`.** Without it the BPMN runtime sees a literal string (`"vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"`) and binds it as-is to the activity input — `flow validate` passes; the failure surfaces only at `flow debug`. There is no `nodes.X.output.Y` syntax — that is an invention that silently ships as a literal string. See [node-output-wiring.md](../../../../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the per-field-type rule and the full failure-mode table (MST-9107).
216	
217	### Step 6 — Configure the node
218	
219	**Run `is resources describe` (Step 3) before this step.** The full metadata tells you which fields are required, what types they expect, and which need reference resolution. Do not guess field names or skip the metadata check — required fields missing from `--detail` cause runtime errors that `flow validate` does not catch.
220	
221	> **Re-configure is full rebuild, not partial merge — every `--detail` field omitted gets dropped.** Each `node configure` call constructs a fresh `inputs.detail` object (`connector-service.ts:792-803`) and a fresh `essentialConfiguration` blob from `--detail` only. Anything not in this call's `--detail` is dropped from the rewritten flow:
222	>
223	> | If you omit on re-configure | What happens |
224	> |---|---|
225	> | `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` | Field is removed from `inputs.detail` (the prior values are NOT preserved) |
226	> | `filter` | `savedFilterTrees` is omitted from the `=jsonString:` blob; `queryParameters.<filterParamName>` is not re-derived |
227	> | `customFieldsRequestDetails` | Resets to `null` inside the `=jsonString:` blob |
228	>
229	> **Rule:** always re-pass the full intended `--detail` shape — connection plumbing + every parameter bucket + filter tree + customFieldsRequestDetails — even when changing one field. The CLI does not read the prior `inputs.detail` to fill gaps.
230	
231	#### Step 6a — Detect FilterBuilder parameters
232	
233	Before writing `--detail`, scan the operation's `parameters[]` (from Step 3 / `registry get`) for any entry with `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. This applies to **any** operation, not only List operations — connectors render the FilterBuilder UI for any param flagged this way.
234	
235	For every match:
236	
237	- That parameter's `name` is the connector-specific filter input — most commonly `where`, sometimes `q` (Salesforce), sometimes another name. Do not assume `where`.
238	- **Pass a structured filter tree under `--detail.filter`** — the CLI compiles it into both halves of the contract: the runtime CEQL string at `inputs.detail.queryParameters.<name>` *and* the design-time tree at `inputs.detail.configuration.essentialConfiguration.savedFilterTrees.<name>`. Studio Web reads the latter to render the FilterBuilder UI; only `--detail.filter` populates that side.
239	- **Do not pass a raw CEQL string under `--detail.queryParameters.<name>`.** It populates only the runtime half — debug runs succeed but the FilterBuilder UI shows `undefined` when the activity is reopened in SW. The CLI rejects this at configure time.
240	- **A dynamic operand in the tree works**: `"value": {"value": "=js:$vars...", "isLiteral": false}` — the CLI compiles it to a `{var_…}` placeholder plus `inputs.detail.filterVariables` the runtime resolves.
241	- **When a CEQL string is authored anyway** (e.g. a `queryExpression` written directly into the `.flow`): field names bare, values single-quoted — `` `accountNumber = '${$vars...}'` ``, never `'accountNumber' = '...'`. The whole value MUST start with `` =js:` `` and end with `` ` `` when it interpolates: `` "=js:`invoiceNumber = '${$vars...}'`" ``. A plain string containing `${…}` is never resolved — the query silently matches nothing. Copy-paste template, operator aliases, and the error→fix table → [Hand-authored CEQL strings](#hand-authored-ceql-strings) below.
242	- Tree shape, operator table, examples → [uipath-platform — Filter Trees (CEQL)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/activities.md#filter-trees-ceql).
243	
244	If the operation has no FilterBuilder parameter, server-side filtering is not supported — pass no `filter` and filter downstream (e.g. with a Script node).
245	
246	**Dynamic-entity connectors (e.g. Data Service).** Their FilterBuilder params take `--detail.filter` like every other connector. Always set the entity name in the same `node configure` call (`pathParameters.entityName` on Data Service) — the CLI runs the connector's schema-fetch action from it and resolves the entity's real fields. Field ids in the tree must match that schema exactly. Matching is case-sensitive: `InvoiceNumber` does not match `invoiceNumber`. Read the exact names from `uip df entities list --output json` (entity `Id`) plus `uip df entities get <entity-id> --output json` (field names). An unmatched leaf is dropped without an error — `node configure` reports Success and the filter is lost or malformed. See [Common Errors](#common-errors).
247	
248	##### Hand-authored CEQL strings
249	
250	Preference order. Do not skip step 1.
251	
252	1. **`node configure --detail.filter`** — pass a structured tree. The CLI compiles the CEQL for you. Use this for every literal filter. It does not report a leaf whose field id the entity schema does not match — it drops that leaf (see Step 6a).
253	2. **Hand-authored `=js:` string** — use only when a runtime value forces it, and only from the template below. Nothing validates the string: `flow validate` passes it through and IS faults at `flow debug` with `[102003]`.
254	
255	Canonical template for a dynamic value:
256	
257	```text
258	=js:"accountNumber = '" + String($vars.<node>.output.<field>) + "'"
259	```
260	
261	Single quotes delimit a value. Double quotes mark a column reference to the CEQL parser.
262	
263	**Anti-patterns.** Match the IS error text, then apply the corrected form.
264	
265	| Wrong form | IS error text | Corrected form |
266	|---|---|---|
267	| `'accountNumber' = 'ACC123'` — field name quoted | `Expected a field name expression but got 'StringValue'` | `accountNumber = 'ACC123'` |
268	| `` =js:"accountNumber = \"" + String(v) + "\"" `` — value double-quoted | `Unsupported value expression 'Column' on field 'accountNumber'` | `` =js:"accountNumber = '" + String(v) + "'" `` |
269	| `accountNumber eq 'ACC123'` — OData alias | `[102003] Integration Services bad request` | `accountNumber = 'ACC123'` |
270	
271	CEQL rejects OData aliases. Map them:
272	
273	| OData alias | CEQL operator |
274	|---|---|
275	| `eq` | `=` |
276	| `ne` | `!=` |
277	| `gt` | `>` |
278	| `ge` | `>=` |
279	| `lt` | `<` |
280	| `le` | `<=` |
281	
282	Full operator table → [uipath-platform — Filter Trees (CEQL)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/activities.md#filter-trees-ceql).
283	
284	#### Step 6b — Run configure
285	
286	After adding the node with `uip maestro flow node add`, configure it with the resolved connection and field values.
287	
288	**Concrete activity** (Jira `curated_create_issue` — object encoded in node type):
289	
290	```bash
291	uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> \
292	  --detail '{"connectionId": "<id>", "folderKey": "<key>", "method": "POST", "endpoint": "/issues", "bodyParameters": {"fields.project.key": "ENGCE", "fields.issuetype.id": "10004"}}' \
293	  --output json
294	```
295	
296	**Generic activity, list** (Salesforce `list-records` against Opportunity — object selected at configure time, no per-record input):
297	
298	```bash
299	uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> \
300	  --detail '{"connectionId": "<id>", "folderKey": "<key>", "method": "GET", "endpoint": "/Opportunity", "objectName": "Opportunity"}' \
301	  --output json
302	```
303	
304	**Generic activity, retrieve-by-id** (Salesforce `get-record` against Account — object plus a path parameter for the record ID):
305	
306	```bash
307	uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> \
308	  --detail '{"connectionId": "<id>", "folderKey": "<key>", "method": "GETBYID", "endpoint": "/Account/{accountId}", "objectName": "Account", "pathParameters": {"accountId": "001KY000007uI02YAE"}}' \
309	  --output json
310	```
311	
312	Path-parameterized GETs are a distinct shape from list/query: `endpoint` carries `{<placeholder>}` tokens and `pathParameters` supplies the values. Resolve the ID via `is resources run list <connector-key> <objectName>` (Step 4) — never paste IDs across connections (see [reference-resolution.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/reference-resolution.md#reference-ids-are-connection-scoped-critical)).
313	
314	The `objectName` field is required for generic nodes (see "Generic vs Concrete Activities" above). The CLI fails fast with a runnable hint when it's missing on a generic node. For concrete nodes the field is ignored if supplied.
315	
316	**Source of truth for `method` and `endpoint`** — pick either (both read the same upstream IS metadata):
317	
318	- `registry get` (Step 2) → `connectorMethodInfo.method` and `connectorMethodInfo.path` — populated for **concrete** activities only.
319	- `is resources describe <connector-key> <objectName> --operation <Op>` (Step 3) → `availableOperations[].method` and `availableOperations[].path` — works for both, and is the only source for **generic** activities.
320	
321	> **Method label — pass the IS describe value verbatim.** `is resources describe` sometimes returns synthesized IS-side labels (notably `"GETBYID"` for path-parameterized retrieve operations). The CLI accepts both standard HTTP verbs (`GET`, `POST`, …) and IS-side labels (`GETBYID`) — copy `operation.method` from `is resources describe` as-is and the CLI normalizes to the underlying HTTP verb internally. Don't translate by hand.
322	
323	> **`flow validate` cross-checks `method` against the activity's `operation`.** If the value you pass disagrees with the operation baked into the node by `node add` (e.g. `method: "POST"` on a Retrieve activity), validate fails with `HTTP method "<X>" does not match operation "<Y>". Expected "<Z>"`. This catches stale copy-paste — fix by re-reading `operation.method` from `is resources describe` against the right `--operation`.
324	
325	Body field names in `bodyParameters` come from `inputDefinition.fields[].name` (`registry get`, concrete only) or `requestFields[].name` (`is resources describe`, both).
326	
327	> **Array fields — `[*]` indicates an array.** `[*]` in `requestFields[].name` (or `inputDefinition.fields[].name`) marks the field as an array; `dataType` identifies the element type. **Supported only when `[*]` is the name suffix.** Any name containing `[*].` (path segments after the `[*]`, e.g. `addresses[*].zipCode`, `contacts[*].emails[*]`) is not authorable — the canvas UI does not emit these shapes. The rule below covers `bodyParameters`, `queryParameters`, and `pathParameters`.
328	>
329	> | `requestFields[].name` | `dataType` | Authoring shape in `inputs.detail` |
330	> |---|---|---|
331	> | `fields.labels[*]` | `string` | `"fields.labels": "=js:(['shield', 'p0'])"` |
332	> | `fields.components_arrayRemap_name[*]` | `string` | `"fields.components_arrayRemap_name": "=js:(['IS Runtime'])"` |
333	> | `users[*]` | `string` | `"users": "=js:(['U123ABC', 'U456DEF'])"` |
334	>
335	> **Strip `[*]` from the key; pass a `=js:` expression returning the array.**  The runtime rejects any key containing the literal `[*]` substring as unknown (regardless of value shape), so pass the stripped form in your `node configure --detail` payload. **A literal JSON array (`"users": ["U123ABC", "U456DEF"]`) passes `node configure` and `flow validate` but does not bind — the field round-trips empty.** **Distinct from `customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues`**, where `[*]` is encoded as `_array` — see Step 6c.
336	>
337	> **Expression values.** The serializer is purely structural (dot-expansion only; no expression evaluation, no type coercion). Choose the authoring shape based on what the expression returns at runtime:
338	>
339	> | Expression resolves to | Authoring shape | Example |
340	> |---|---|---|
341	> | The whole array | `"<field>": "=<expr>"` | `"fields.labels": "=js:$vars.allTags"` |
342	> | A single element to wrap | `"<field>": "=js:([<expr>])"` | `"fields.labels": "=js:([$vars.priorityTag])"` |
343	
344	> **Connector output shape — derive it from `connectorMethodInfo`, never from vendor-API intuition.**
345	>
346	> | `connectorMethodInfo.operation` | `output` at runtime | Loop / binding shape |
347	> |---|---|---|
348	> | `list` | bare **array**; `outputResponseDefinition.fields` describes one element | `"collection": "=js:$vars.<node>.output"` |
349	> | anything else (`retrieve`, `create`, `update`, …) | single **object** matching those fields | `=js:$vars.<node>.output.<field>` |
350	>
351	> Ignore `outputDefinition.output.type` — it says `"object"` even for `list` operations, where the actual output type is an array.
352	
353	The command populates `inputs.detail` and creates workflow-level `bindings` entries. Use **resolved IDs** from Step 4, not display names. For FilterBuilder params, see Step 6a.
354	
355	When inspecting the resulting `.flow`, note that the folder field is named `connectionFolderKey` in `inputs.detail`. The CLI `--detail` input accepts `folderKey` for convenience, then serializes the `.flow` field expected by validation. Do not hand-edit this field — `inputs.detail` is CLI-owned (see [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node)); re-run `node configure` to change it.
356	
357	> **Do not use `filterExpression`** — that field is the trigger / JMESPath path. See [connector-trigger/impl.md](../connector-trigger/impl.md#filter-trees).
358	
359	> **Shell quoting tip:** For complex `--detail` JSON, write it to a temp file: `uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> --detail "$(cat /tmp/detail.json)" --output json`

361	#### Step 6c — Populate custom fields (api-type ObjectActions)
362	
363	A connector activity has a **parent-field-driven schema** when its valid input fields are not fixed in static metadata but are computed at design time by running an api-type ObjectAction against the IS Element Service. Examples: Jira's `Create Issue` schema depends on the project + issue type; Snowflake's `executeQuery` response columns depend on the SQL string; Dataservice V3's entity field set depends on `tenantEntityName`. The activity persists the parent-field values in `essentialConfiguration.customFieldsRequestDetails` so the runtime can replay the schema-fetch ObjectAction on each invocation. The CLI passes this through verbatim.
364	
365	**How DAP determines support — check both metadata locations.** An api-type action may live at either:
366	
367	- Top-level `objectActions[]` with PascalCase `ActionType: "Api"` (older shape, e.g. Jira `GenerateSchema`)
368	- `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` with lowercase `actionType: "api"` (newer shape, e.g. Dataservice V3 `FetchObjectMetadataTenant`)
369	
370	The dispatcher matches `ObjectActionType.Api === 'api'` (case-sensitive lowercase string) — both shapes go through the same `_processCustomFieldsRequestAction` code path with no per-connector branching. Always inspect both locations from `registry get` output before deciding the connector has none.
371	
372	The matching action is then selected by one of two rule sources:
373	
374	- **`source: field`** — the action's `rules[].refFieldName` are satisfied by user-supplied `-f, --field` values (typically SQL-style query connectors where the query string is the parent field).
375	- **`source: method`** — the action is declared at the operation level and matched against the operation's HTTP method (typically CRUD activities).
376	
377	**Examples of supported activities.** The list below is illustrative, not exhaustive — DAP's actual support set evolves with connector metadata. Always confirm by inspecting `objectActions[]` / `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` from `registry get` for the specific (connector, object, activity) you're configuring.
378	
379	| Connector key | Object | Activity / Action | HTTP | Source |
380	|---|---|---|---|---|
381	| `uipath-microsoft-azureapplicationinsights` | `executeQuery` | `generateSchema` | — | field |
382	| `uipath-salesforce-sfdc` | `curated_soqlQuery` | `generateSchema` | — | field |
383	| `uipath-workday-workdayrest` | `wql` | `generateSchema` | — | field |
384	| `uipath-oracle-netsuite` | `executeSuiteQL` | `generateSchema` | — | field |
385	| `uipath-snowflake-snowflake` | `executeQuery` | `generateSchema` | — | field |
386	| `uipath-atlassian-jira` | `curated_create_issue` | Create Issue | POST | method |
387	| `uipath-atlassian-jira` | `curated_edit_issue` | Update Issue | PUT | method |
388	| `uipath-atlassian-jira` | `curated_get_issue` | Get Issue | GETBYID | method |
389	| `uipath-uipath-dataservice` | `CreateEntityRecordCurated` | Create Entity Record | POST | method |
390	| `uipath-uipath-dataservice` | `QueryEntityRecordsCurated` | Query Entity Records | POST | method |
391	| `uipath-mailchimp-mailchimp` | `list_members_curated_dynamic::members` | Add Subscriber | POST | method |

395	
396	If neither metadata location contains an `actionType: "api"` / `ActionType: "Api"` entry for the activity you're configuring, it has no parent-field-driven schema — omit `customFieldsRequestDetails` (CLI emits `null`).
397	
398	Each api-type entry has `name` (the `ObjectActionName`) and `apiConfiguration.{url,body}` with `{token}` placeholders — those tokens name the parent fields whose values must be in `parameterValues`.
399	
400	**Script:** `python3 scripts/encode_parameter_values.py --field '<parentField>=<value>' [--field ...] [--object-action-name <ObjectActionName>] [--bucket bodyParameters|queryParameters|pathParameters]` emits `parameterValues` as encoded tuples plus the raw-keyed `runtimeParameters` copy, so both halves of the contract go into `--detail`. `--encode-only '<token>'` prints one encoded key. Which parent fields the activity needs still comes from the metadata you read above.
401	
402	**Token encoding rule.** Tokens are encoded via `NamingHelper.getValidIdentifier` (the IS-side identifier sanitizer) before being used as `parameterValues` keys, so they match design-property names at lookup time. Substitutions (applied longest-first):
403	
404	| Match in token | Encoded as |
405	|---|---|
406	| `:::` | `_sub_` |
407	| `[*]` | `_array` |
408	| `::` | `_sub_` |
409	| `.` | `_sub_` |
410	
411	Examples: `fields.project.key` → `fields_sub_project_sub_key`; `items[*]` → `items_array`; `tenantEntityName` → `tenantEntityName` (unchanged). When in doubt, inspect a working `.flow` for the encoded form.
412	
413	> **`customFieldsRequestDetails` is COMPLEMENTARY to `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters`, not a substitute.** Same parent-field values must appear in BOTH places, with different keys:
414	>
415	> | Location | Purpose | Key shape |
416	> |---|---|---|
417	> | `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` | Runtime input — what the connector actually sends to its API | **Raw** field names (e.g. `fields.project.key`, `tenantEntityName`) |
418	> | `essentialConfiguration.customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues` | Design-time replay cache — drives the parent-field-driven schema fetch when the activity is re-opened or re-validated | **Encoded** keys (e.g. `fields_sub_project_sub_key`, `tenantEntityName`) |
419	>
420	> Concrete (Jira Create Issue): `bodyParameters.fields.project.key = "ENGCE"` AND `parameterValues = [["fields_sub_project_sub_key", "ENGCE"]]`. Concrete (Dataservice V3): `queryParameters.tenantEntityName = ""my-entity""` AND `parameterValues = [["tenantEntityName", ""my-entity""]]`. Dropping the runtime-input copy on the assumption that the cache covers it leaves the runtime with no field value to bind — manifests as `DAP-DT-_2003 refField with name <X> not found` at activity load.
421	
422	**Shape (verified against Solution 386 — Jira Create Issue):**
423	
424	```json
425	"customFieldsRequestDetails": {
426	  "objectActionName": "GenerateSchema",
427	  "parameterValues": [
428	    ["fields_sub_project_sub_key", "ENGCE"],
429	    ["fields_sub_issuetype_sub_id", "3"]
430	  ]
431	}
432	```
433	
434	Rules:
435	
436	- camelCase keys (`objectActionName`, `parameterValues`). PascalCase rejected at validate time.
437	- `parameterValues` is an **array of `[key, value]` tuples** — never an object map. The IS-side serializer emits a `Map<string,string|null>` via `Array.from(entries())`; the CLI rejects object-map form.
438	- Tuple value is `string` or `null`. Use `null` for tokens the user has not yet set.
439	- The CLI does NOT validate ObjectAction existence or token coverage at configure time. **Always run Step 3a first** with the planned parent-field combination — if it errors with `No api-type ObjectAction matched for fields [...]`, the cache you're about to write is wrong (adjust tokens or action name); if it succeeds, the response confirms the action and tokens are real, and you author `customFieldsRequestDetails` from that result, not from memory or doc examples. Read `apiConfiguration.url` / `body` from the matched action (top-level `objectActions[]` OR `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]`) to enumerate required tokens.
440	
441	**CLI invocation — pass BOTH halves.** The runtime input bucket (`bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters`) AND the design-time cache (`customFieldsRequestDetails`) must both appear in the same `--detail`. Omitting the runtime bucket is the most common mistake — the cache alone does not feed the connector at runtime.
